title: Where (and when) to deploy conversational AI first
summary: Your first conversational AI deployment should be simple and boring. Here's how to choose it, and when you're ready to.

-


**Readiness comes before placement:** An agent that can't see the customer will fail on any journey you give it.


-


**Start where mistakes are cheap:** Reversibility matters more than complexity when picking a first deployment.


-


**Baseline first:** Two weeks of before-data is worth more than six months of after-data with nothing to compare.


## Where (and when) to deploy conversational AI first


Most first conversational AI deployments get chosen the same way: Someone pulls the ticket volume report, sorts descending, and picks the top row.


Sure, that makes sense in a lot of situations. It's a defensible instinct and it produces a predictable outcome. The highest-volume contact type is usually the one customers care most about, but that also makes it the worst place to learn.


There’s a right way to go about this, and there’s a right time, too. Let’s get into both of them.


## Where to deploy conversational AI first


Here’s what to think about when choosing your starting place:


1.


**Mistakes are cheap and reversible.** Rescheduling an appointment takes seconds to undo. Reversing a payment takes days and a ticket. Sort candidate journeys by cost of error before you sort by volume.


2.


**The data already exists in one place.** Pick a journey whose context lives in a system your[AI agent](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/ai-agents-explained) can already read. The first deployment shouldn't also be an integration project.


3.


**You're currently failing on speed or availability.**[Consumers rank immediate resolution and speed joint first at 40% each](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/report/great-ai-illusion-why-customers-value-empathy#:~:text=The%20reveal%3A%20Helpful,technology%20at%20all.) , then accuracy and 24/7 availability at 38%. If a journey has a queue or an after-hours gap, AI improves something customers already told you they want.


4.


**A human is nearby.** Start where escalation is easy and well-staffed.


[WestCX runs appointment rescheduling and insurance verification](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report/innovator-1) , both high-volume and reversible.[Eltropy started with balance checks and transaction history](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report/innovator-5) , both read-only.


### Where not to start


-


Anything involving money, health, or a signature.[Consumers pull back sharply](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/report/scale-automation-with-losing-customer-confidence#:~:text=Where%20customer%20confidence,loan%20application%20(54%25)) on payments made on their behalf (56% won't) and loan applications (54% won't).


-


Emotionally loaded contacts. Some complaints need a person. Automating it resolves the ticket but loses the customer.


-


Journeys that cross multiple systems. Save the hard integration for after you've proven the pattern.


-


Anything you can't measure today. If you can't baseline it, you won't be able to defend it.


## When you're ready (4 things to check first)


### Can the agent see the customer?


[84% of brands say their AI can access customer history](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/report/navigating-data-deluge-charting-customer-context#:~:text=Fortunately%2C%20most%20are,their%20AI%20agents.) while only 40% design personalization around it, and 48% name connecting data across channels as their top obstacle.


Devesh Maheshwari, CTO at Lendi Group,[calls fragmentation the data fragment tax](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report/innovator-4) and recommends unifying the real-time data layer before scaling AI. If your first deployment has to ask for an order number your systems already have somewhere, you're testing the wrong thing.


### Is there an exit with context attached?


[63% of consumers want an easy way to escalate at any point](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/report/scale-automation-with-losing-customer-confidence#:~:text=63%25%20want%20a%20quick%2C%20easy%20way%20to%20escalate%20to%20a%20live%20person%20at%20any%20time%20and%2078%25%20say%20they%E2%80%99ve%20tried%20to%20bypass%20AI%20agents%20to%20speak%20directly%20to%20a%20human.) , but only 47% of brands provide one. Worse, 76% of consumers say the human they reach has little or no context.


A deployment without a working handoff doesn't fail gracefully. It fails twice, once with the AI and again with the agent who picks up blind.


### Do you have a baseline?


Capture the current numbers for the specific journey before you automate it:


-


Handle time


-


Resolution rate


-


Repeat contact


-


Abandonment


Two weeks is normally enough.


Without it, you'll have a deployment that might be working but no way to demonstrate it, which is how AI programs lose funding while performing fine.


### Is the scope narrow enough?


[Eltropy's containment numbers](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report/innovator-5) come from voice agents handling balance checks and transaction history at community financial institutions, where voice accounts for 65% of all customer communication. Tightly scoped, high-repetition, clearly bounded.


That scoping is why the number is achievable. A general-purpose agent pointed at everything produces a worse result on every journey.


## Start boring, prove it, then scale


The best first deployment is one nobody will (or should) write a case study about:


-


High repetition


-


Low stakes


-


Data already available


-


A human one click away


We know there’s executive attention on this right now, and that’s not the most glamorous answer. Still, it’s the most practical, and it's the one that leads to a second deployment. The teams that start with their hardest journey tend to spend the following quarter explaining why.
